scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You press one blue button and your vote is recorded. How does an electronic voting machine actually work?

scenes.name: units
scenes.text: An EVM has two parts. A ballot unit where you vote, and a control unit kept with the polling officer.

scenes.name: enable
scenes.text: The officer presses a button to allow one vote. After you vote, it locks until the next voter.

scenes.name: vvpat
scenes.text: A VVPAT printer shows a paper slip with your candidate's symbol for about seven seconds, then drops it into a sealed box.

scenes.name: standalone
scenes.text: As described by the Election Commission, the machines are standalone, not connected to the internet or any network.

scenes.name: seal
scenes.text: After polling, the units are sealed and kept in guarded strong rooms until counting day.

scenes.name: count
scenes.text: On counting day, the control unit shows totals per candidate, and some VVPAT slips are matched against them.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Press, verify on paper, seal, count. Follow for more on how things really work.
